title: Induction
summary: Magnetic flux and flux linkage, Faraday’s and Lenz’s laws, induced e.m.f. in moving conductors and rotating coils, and how generators produce alternating current.

keyterms.definition: Φ = BA cos θ, where θ is the angle between B and the normal to the area; unit weber (Wb).
Total flux through a coil of N turns: NΦ.
Induced e.m.f. equals the rate of change of flux linkage: ε = −NΔΦ/Δt.
The induced current flows so as to oppose the change that produces it; a consequence of energy conservation.
E.m.f. induced in a rod of length L moving at v through field B: ε = BvL.
A coil rotating in a magnetic field, producing a sinusoidal alternating e.m.f.
Induced currents circulating in bulk conductors, which oppose motion and dissipate energy.
Unit of magnetic flux: 1 Wb = 1 T m².

questions.text: A 0.40 T field passes perpendicularly through a loop of area 0.050 m². The flux is ___ Wb.

questions.prompt: A 200-turn coil has its flux changed from 0.020 Wb to zero in 0.10 s. The average induced e.m.f. is

questions.statement: A steady, unchanging magnetic field through a stationary coil induces an e.m.f.
questions.explanation: An e.m.f. is induced only when the flux linkage changes.

questions.prompt: A magnet’s north pole is pushed into a coil. By Lenz’s law, the end of the coil nearest the magnet becomes
options: a north pole, repelling the magnet
a south pole, attracting the magnet
questions.explanation: The induced current opposes the change (the approach), so a north pole forms and repels the magnet.

questions.text: A 0.30 m rod moves at 5.0 m s⁻¹ perpendicular to a 0.20 T field. The induced e.m.f. is ___ V.

questions.prompt: Match each idea to its description.
questions.explanation: Faraday gives the magnitude; the minus sign (Lenz) gives the direction.

questions.statement: Lenz’s law is a consequence of conservation of energy.
questions.explanation: If the induced current aided the change, energy would be created from nothing.

questions.prompt: Which change would NOT increase the e.m.f. induced by moving a magnet into a coil?
options: Using thicker wire with the same turns
questions.explanation: ε depends on N and the rate of change of flux; wire thickness changes resistance (current) but not e.m.f.

questions.prompt: A copper disc swinging between magnet poles stops quickly. This is due to
questions.explanation: Induced eddy currents oppose the relative motion (Lenz), transferring kinetic energy to internal energy; used in magnetic braking.

questions.prompt: Order the reasoning for a falling magnet slowing in a copper tube.
items: The magnet falls and the flux through the tube changes
E.m.f.s are induced in the copper
Eddy currents flow in the tube
Their magnetic field opposes the magnet’s motion
questions.explanation: Energy is dissipated in the tube, so the magnet reaches a low terminal speed.

questions.prompt: A coil rotates at constant rate in a uniform field. The induced e.m.f. is maximum when the plane of the coil is
questions.explanation: When the plane is parallel to B the flux is zero but changing fastest, so ε is maximum.

questions.statement: When the flux through a rotating coil is maximum, the induced e.m.f. is zero.
questions.explanation: At maximum flux the rate of change of flux is momentarily zero.

questions.text: If a generator coil’s rotation frequency doubles, the peak e.m.f. is multiplied by ___.
questions.explanation: Peak ε = NBAω, so doubling ω doubles the peak e.m.f. (and the frequency of the a.c.).

questions.prompt: A graph of flux linkage against time for a rotating coil is a sine curve. The e.m.f.–time graph is
options: a cosine curve (90° out of phase), with minus sign
questions.explanation: ε = −d(NΦ)/dt; the derivative of a sine is a cosine, shifted by a quarter period.

questions.prompt: Match each feature to its effect.

pairs.right: Larger peak e.m.f. and higher frequency

questions.explanation: Generator design choices change the output.

questions.prompt: A rectangular coil of 50 turns and area 0.020 m² rotates at 10 rad s⁻¹ in a 0.50 T field. The peak e.m.f. is

questions.statement: A bigger current drawn from a generator makes it harder to turn.
questions.explanation: The larger induced current produces a larger opposing force (Lenz), so more work is needed: electrical energy comes from mechanical work.

questions.text: The unit T m² is called the ___.
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux Φ = BA is measured in webers.

questions.prompt: A rod is pulled across rails in a magnetic field, completing a circuit. The force needed to keep it at constant speed
options: equals the magnetic force on the induced current
questions.explanation: The induced current gives a force BIL opposing motion; at constant velocity the pull balances it, and its power equals the electrical power.
